paragraphs: The regular Zoomer shares its movement state machine with other crawlers.
InitAI_Zoomer_MZoomer chooses its starting orientation; MainAI_Crawlers
dispatches the handler installed by the orientation's animation script.
InitAI_Waver splits the regional horizontal speed and chooses its direction.
MainAI_Waver moves horizontally, derives vertical distance from a wave phase,
and coordinates steady/spinning animation scripts through a completion flag.
Population parameter 1 bit 0 selects left (0) or right (1), not a speed index.
Prepare enemy graphics/palettes and clear the base runtime enemy records before
Initialise_Enemies fills population slots and calls Init AI. The enemy set and
population are separate resources. Reset room-level enemy hooks and bookkeeping,
process the set and load tile data into RAM, then clear inherited sprite objects.
Door transitions have already loaded enemy VRAM graphics on an earlier path.
Zero $0800 bytes of base enemy records: each word write advances X twice and
decrements the byte counter twice. Then inspect the first population ID.
An immediate $FFFF skips enemy-set processing; a nonempty population processes
the graphics/palette set before returning. This does not call enemy Init AI.
Enter with word-sized registers. First clear $1400 words ($2800 bytes) from
EnemyTileData at $7E:7000 through $7E:97FF, then reset projectile bookkeeping.
For each $10-byte population record, fill a $40-byte runtime slot from header
defaults and placement fields, expose the slot in EnemyIndex and call Init AI.
The generic init word at population offset $06 first occupies Enemy.instList;
some Init AI, including Zoomer, reads it as flags rather than an address.
The AI can change these fields. After it returns, reset/select the placeholder
spritemap, advance both cursors and stop at $FFFF. Only the nonempty-list tail
records FirstFreeEnemyIndex, the listed count and the terminator's kill byte.
The earlier JSL supplied the long return frame for Init AI's RTL. Select the
AI data bank with the swapped-word push and two bank pulls, then tail-jump
through EnemyAIPointer. The caller restores its saved bank and X/Y cursors.
Match the population's enemy ID against four-byte enemy-set entries. Prior
entries contribute tile counts from their header size divided by $20. A match
supplies the palette index and accumulated graphics offset for the runtime
slot and its spawn-data mirror. A missing match uses offset zero and $0A00
palette attributes. Population position/parameters are not graphics metadata.
Build separate active and interaction lists of runtime slot offsets, each ending
in $FFFF. Scan 32 base records at $40-byte intervals, skipping empty/respawn
slots and clearing deletion-marked IDs. Ordinary processing allows property
$0800 or frozen-AI bit $0004 to bypass viewport culling; property $0400 omits
the slot from the logical interaction list without omitting its AI.
The global offscreen override takes a different scan with no viewport tests.
The override still skips empty/respawn/deleted slots. It also writes each active
slot into InteractiveEnemyIndices at the active-list offset before testing
$0400. The separate interaction cursor controls accepted logical insertions and
the final sentinel; retain the distinction between this extra store and that
logical list. This path is not the ordinary visibility path with one flag changed.
Consume the active list selected earlier, performing collision checks, AI,
script updates and drawing-queue eligibility as separate stages. Do not equate
an active slot with an interactive or drawable one. The early zero-population
path still reaches sprite-object handling and collision-bookkeeping cleanup.
Global frozen time and the per-enemy frozen-AI flag are different conditions.
Only branches arriving here apply this pre-AI paralysis skip. Intangible slots,
nonzero invincibility timers and the debug interaction bypass instead enter
.interactEnd directly. The later .processAIEnd paralysis/death test is separate.
Enemy.AI = 0 selects the main-AI word at header offset $18. Otherwise select
one plus the zero-based index of the lowest set bit, then read $18 + 2*index:
bit 0 selects grapple AI ($1A), bit 1 hurt AI ($1C), bit 2 frozen AI ($1E).
Higher bits continue the same arithmetic without a validity mask. The earlier
global frozen-time path bypasses this selector and uses header offset $20.
The caller's JSL supplied the long return frame. Refresh the pointer's bank,
select the enemy's data bank and tail-jump through EnemyAIPointer. Its RTL
returns after that JSL; the caller restores the header bank and skips over
this inline helper before rechecking frozen time and processing instructions.
Extended spritemaps bypass the ordinary visibility helper. Other slots must
pass its radius-padded X and fixed-margin Y tests. Then property bits $0100/
$0200 and drawing-disable bit 0 can still prevent queue insertion.
The layer queue contains slot-offset words for a later drawing pass, not OAM.
Advance the selected enemy's script only when AI bit $0004 is clear and the
pre-decremented instruction timer becomes zero. A negative script word is a
bank-local command; a nonnegative word begins a four-byte duration/spritemap
record. The caller supplies EnemyAIPointer's bank byte; this routine sets its
command word and the script data bank. Enter with the expected word register mode.
PHK/PEA create a long return to the fetch loop. Commands normally RTL there,
but terminating commands replace the return word to reach the shared exit.
A timer initially zero wraps to $FFFF on decrement; it is not an immediate tick.
Accept the fetched word as duration, install the following spritemap word and
advance the saved cursor by four bytes. Set properties2 bit $8000 on this path;
the nonzero-timer path clears it. Frozen-AI and terminating-command exits do
not perform that same marker update.
Return A=0/Z set when these viewport tests pass, A=1/Z clear otherwise.
Horizontal bounds include XHitboxRadius; vertical bounds use Y+8 and camera
Y+$F8, not YHitboxRadius. These match the ordinary activity scan's tests.
Comparisons branch on the subtraction result's N flag as written; this is
not a general-purpose signed-coordinate rectangle test.
Append the current runtime slot offset to the queue selected by Enemy.layer.
The layer indexes an eight-word base-address table; queue sizes are byte counts
and increase by two per appended word. This routine does not draw the sprite
or append a sentinel, and has no layer/capacity bounds check.
Y points to the destination parameter word after the fetched command. Replace
Y with that word and RTL to the interpreter loop, which fetches at the new cursor.
Set Enemy.loopCounter from the parameter word and advance Y by two.
This loop counter is separate from Enemy.instTimer's graphical/wait duration.
Pre-decrement the loop-counter word. A nonzero result reuses the goto command
with the current target parameter; zero skips that parameter and continues.
Neither path ends this interpreter call or changes the spritemap directly.
Y starts after this command word. Rewind it by two and save the sleep command's
address in Enemy.instList. Replace the interpreter loop's return word with its
shared exit word, keeping the synthetic bank byte, then RTL out of this call.
This command does not set Enemy.instTimer or change the spritemap.
Load Enemy.instTimer from the duration parameter, save the cursor after it and
terminate this interpreter call by replacing the synthetic return word.
The current spritemap is retained. This differs from a graphical record,
which installs a new spritemap and performs the graphical-update marker write.
Set property $0200 and exit this interpreter call through a replaced return word.
The command does not clear Enemy.ID itself. Activity selection later removes
deletion-marked slots; drawing eligibility also rejects that property bit.

lines.comment: Select bank $A0 for enemy headers and enemy-loading helpers.
Use word-sized registers while preparing the room's enemy resources.
Load the optional debug enemy-set data on this build path.
Clear the debug-only enemy frozen-time setting.
Clear the previous room's boss identifier.
Select the bank of the default no-op graphics hook.
Start replacing the graphics hook's long pointer.
Select the no-op RTL routine's word address.
Finish installing a harmless default enemy-graphics hook.
Set the default enemy BG2 tilemap size to $0800 bytes.
Repeat the earlier BossID reset.
Clear enemy records and process the room's enemy graphics/palette set.
Load enemy tile data into the RAM staging buffer.
Reset the enemy tile-transfer source address.
Allow Samus/projectile interactions for the new room.
Clear sprite objects inherited from the previous room.
Use word-sized stores and counters for the base enemy-record clear.
Fill the runtime enemy records with zero words.
Count $0800 bytes of base enemy-record storage.
Begin at the first enemy slot.
Clear this word, not just an individual enemy ID.
Advance the destination cursor by one of this word's two bytes.
Consume one of the two cleared bytes from the remaining count.
Finish advancing past the word just cleared.
Consume its second byte from the remaining count.
Continue until all $0800 bytes have been cleared.
Inspect the room's population after clearing every base enemy slot.
Read its first enemy ID word.
An immediate $FFFF means an empty population.
Only a nonempty population processes the enemy set on this path.
Empty populations return without calling the set processor.
Load palettes and enemy-loading metadata from the enemy set.
Count $1400 word writes; unlike the earlier clear, this is not a byte count.
Begin at the EnemyTileData buffer's first byte.
Use a zero word for the tile/extra-enemy RAM clear.
Clear the next word in the $7E:7000..97FF region.
Advance by one of the word's two bytes.
Advance by its second byte.
Consume one word write from the counter, not two bytes.
Repeat for $1400 words, clearing $2800 bytes in total.
Select bank $A0 for fixed enemy-header fields.
Re-establish word-sized registers for header and population processing.
Reset the room's count of killed enemies.
Reset global offscreen-enemy processing for the new room.
Start clearing the extra projectile area from its last word.
Clear an extra enemy-projectile bookkeeping word.
Walk backwards through that area in two-byte steps.
Start at the last killed-enemy-index word.
Use $FFFF as the no-killed-enemy index sentinel.
Reset this projectile's killed-enemy index.
Continue until the killed-enemy-index list is reset.
Start at the first population record.
Read the first population ID, before attempting any enemy Init AI.
An immediate $FFFF selects the early empty-population exit.
Do not run the slot loop or terminator-tail assignments for an empty list.
Use runtime enemy slot offset zero for the first population record.
Match this enemy ID to the enemy set's graphics and palette metadata.
Keep the population cursor while X temporarily selects the enemy header.
Read this placement's fixed enemy-header ID.
Use that ID as the bank-$A0 header pointer.
Read the header's X hitbox radius.
Copy the X radius into the current runtime slot.
Read the header's Y hitbox radius.
Copy the Y radius into the current runtime slot.
Read the header's initial health word.
Copy header health before running enemy-specific Init AI.
Read the header's layer byte.
Discard its neighboring byte.
Set the runtime drawing layer.
Read the AI bank byte together with the neighboring hurt-AI-time byte.
Store that byte pair in the word-sized Enemy.bank field.
Read the header's boss identifier.
A zero identifier does not replace the global BossID.
Keep the nonzero boss identifier from this enemy header.
Recover the population cursor for copying placement fields.
Read the population's enemy-header ID again.
Install that ID in the runtime slot.
Read the population X position.
Set the enemy's initial X coordinate.
Read the population Y position.
Set the enemy's initial Y coordinate.
Read the population's generic initialisation word at record offset $06.
Seed Enemy.instList; Init AI may interpret this word as a parameter, not a pointer.
Read the placement's main property flags.
Install those flags before Init AI runs.
Read the placement's extra property flags.
Install those extra flags before Init AI runs.
Read population parameter 1 at record offset $0C.
Pass it to Init AI through Enemy.init0.
Read population parameter 2 at record offset $0E.
Pass it to Init AI through Enemy.init1.
Start the enemy frame counter at zero.
Start the instruction loop counter at zero.
Prime the instruction timer with one tick.
Store the timer before the enemy-specific initialisation call.
Reset the frame counter a second time.
Record spawn data on the optional debug build path.
Preserve the population cursor across Init AI.
Preserve the runtime slot cursor across Init AI.
Expose the current slot offset through EnemyIndex.
Use the installed enemy ID to find its fixed header.
Read the Init AI word at enemy-header offset $12.
Store the word portion of the dynamic Init AI pointer.
Read the AI bank and adjacent header byte.
Complete the pointer's bank byte; the indirect long jump uses three bytes.
Preserve the header data bank across the enemy's own AI bank.
Supply a long return frame before the helper tail-jumps into Init AI.
Restore the enemy-header data bank after Init AI returns with RTL.
Recover the runtime slot cursor.
Recover the population-record cursor.
Clear the spritemap field after Init AI, not before it.
Inspect the current properties after Init AI may have changed them.
Bit $2000 requests the placeholder spritemap path.
Without that bit, leave the just-cleared spritemap value at zero.
Default to the ordinary empty spritemap.
Check the current extra properties for an extended spritemap.
Bit $0004 chooses the extended empty spritemap.
Select the extended empty spritemap when requested.
Install the selected empty spritemap after initialisation.
Advance from this runtime slot to the next slot.
Runtime enemy records have a $40-byte stride.
Keep Y as the runtime-slot offset.
Advance the corresponding population-record cursor.
Population records have a separate $10-byte stride.
Keep X as the population-list cursor.
Read the next population ID.
Stop at the $FFFF list terminator.
Initialise the next listed enemy when the terminator is not reached.
Record the first slot offset after the listed enemies.
Begin dividing that byte offset by $40 to obtain the listed count.
Store the listed count after six right shifts.
Read the word after the $FFFF terminator through the X-position field alias.
Keep only the trailing required-kill-count byte.
Store that count only after a nonempty population has been processed.
Read the current enemy's bank byte and its neighboring stored byte.
Move the bank byte into the word's high byte for the two pulls.
Push both bytes for selecting the Init AI data bank.
Discard the neighboring byte with the first bank pull.
Select the enemy's AI bank with the second pull.
Tail-jump through the long pointer; Init AI's RTL uses the earlier JSL frame.
Use bank $A0 for enemy records and header constants.
Use word-sized registers for slot offsets and list entries.
Start scanning at runtime slot offset zero.
Reset the active-list insertion cursor, measured in bytes.
Reset the separate interaction-list insertion cursor.
Check the global override for processing offscreen slots.
Use the alternate scan, which skips the normal viewport tests.
Restore the current slot offset before reading its fields.
Read this slot's enemy-header ID.
Skip empty runtime slots.
Recognize the respawn-placeholder enemy ID.
Skip that placeholder rather than scheduling its AI.
Read the current slot's main property flags.
Bit $0200 requests deletion.
Only undeleted slots continue to activity checks.
Remove a deletion-marked slot by clearing its ID.
Do not add the cleared slot to either list.
Bit $0800 bypasses viewport culling for this enemy.
Schedule offscreen-enabled enemies without testing their position.
Read the enemy's AI-selection flags.
The frozen-AI bit also bypasses normal viewport culling.
Keep frozen enemies scheduled even outside the viewport.
Begin the horizontal test with the enemy's X position.
Include its X hitbox radius at the left viewport boundary.
Compare that right edge against the camera's X origin.
Reject the slot when this comparison's subtraction result is negative.
Use a $100-pixel viewport width.
Pad the far horizontal boundary by the same X radius.
Reject the slot when it lies beyond that padded boundary.
Use the enemy's Y position for the vertical tests.
Allow eight pixels above the camera's Y origin.
Reject the slot on the upper vertical test.
Use camera Y plus $F8 for the lower vertical boundary.
Reject the slot on the lower vertical test.
Append the runtime slot offset, not an enemy-header pointer.
Use the active list's own byte insertion cursor.
Store one word in the active-enemy list.
Commit the two-byte active-list cursor advance.
Bit $0400 excludes this active enemy from the interaction list.
Keep its AI eligible even though it is not added for interactions.
Use the interaction list's independent byte cursor.
Append the same runtime slot offset to the interaction list.
Commit that list's two-byte cursor advance.
Advance by one $40-byte runtime enemy record.
Stop after the $0800-byte area containing 32 base slots.
Continue scanning the next slot.
Terminate both logical lists with a $FFFF word.
Place the active-list terminator after its last inserted entry.
Place the interaction-list terminator using its own cursor.
Scan every base slot on the global offscreen-processing path.
Still skip empty slots despite the global override.
Still skip respawn placeholders.
The global override does not bypass deletion handling.
Clear a deletion-marked slot's ID.
Use the active insertion cursor on this alternate path.
Append this slot to the active list.
Also write at that active offset in the interaction array; its logical cursor is separate.
Advance only the active list's cursor at this point.
Test the same $0400 interaction exclusion bit.
Skip logical interaction insertion when that bit is set.
Use the actual interaction-list insertion cursor for the accepted slot.
Append to the logical interaction-list prefix.
Advance the interaction cursor only for that accepted insertion.
Advance the alternate scan by the same $40-byte slot stride.
Use the same 32-slot scan limit.
Continue without any viewport comparison.
Finish the alternate path with the same $FFFF sentinel.
Terminate the active list at its insertion cursor.
Terminate the interaction list at its separate insertion cursor.
Use bank $A0 for fixed enemy-header fields.
Establish word-sized registers for runtime slots and header pointers.
Check the recorded first-free-slot offset before walking the active list.
A nonzero value permits the enemy-processing loop.
Take the shared tail even when no base population was recorded.
Check for a requested enemy shake update.
A $FFFF request means no enemy shake is pending.
Use $40 as the selected enemy's shake duration.
Install that timer in the requested runtime slot.
Consume the pending shake request.
Reset the cursor shared with some interaction routines.
Start consuming the active-list words from offset zero.
Use a byte offset within the active-enemy list.
Read the next runtime enemy-slot offset.
A $FFFF word ends this processing pass.
Run the common tail after the active list ends.
Expose the selected runtime slot through EnemyIndex.
Convert its slot offset into the base enemy-record address.
Cache that address for routines using EnemyDataPointer.
Read the slot's AI bank byte and neighboring stored byte.
Supply the bank part of the shared long AI pointer.
Bit $0400 bypasses this slot's collision-interaction path.
Go directly to the AI path rather than the paralysis precheck.
Check the tangible enemy's invincibility timer.
Only a zero timer reaches the ordinary collision checks.
Tick this timer before checking global frozen time.
Invincibility bypasses collision handling and the paralysis precheck.
Check the debug override for sprite interactions.
The debug override enters the AI path directly.
Check global frozen time before collision handling.
Also include the enemy-specific debug time-freeze setting.
Check global frozen time before collision handling.
Frozen time skips collisions but still reaches the paralysis precheck.
Resolve enemy interactions before choosing its AI handler.
Reload the slot after collision handling.
Check whether collision handling cleared the enemy ID.
A collision-deleted enemy skips AI and drawing-queue insertion.
Inspect the current extra property flags.
Bit $0001 is the paralysis check on paths reaching this block.
Skip AI on this branch; intangible/invincible bypasses did not enter here.
Clear the per-enemy drawing-disable flag on entry to the AI path.
Choose the AI path using global frozen time.
Include the debug enemy time-freeze flag when enabled in this build.
Ordinary time uses the Enemy.AI flag selector.
Use the enemy ID as the bank-$A0 header pointer.
Read the dedicated time-is-frozen callback at header offset $20.
A zero frozen-time callback skips execution for this path.
Use that word with the enemy's AI bank in the long pointer.
Bypass the ordinary AI-bit selector when global time is frozen.
Selector index zero means the header's main-AI word.
Read the enemy's AI-selection bitfield.
A zero bitfield keeps selector index zero.
Count bits starting at one for a nonzero AI bitfield.
Shift the next lowest bit into carry.
Stop on the first set bit, giving it priority over higher bits.
Continue until a set bit is found.
Convert the selector index into a two-byte header displacement.
Add that displacement to the enemy-header address.
Read header offset $18 plus twice the selector index.
Install the selected callback word in the shared AI pointer.
Preserve the header data bank around enemy-specific AI.
Supply the long return frame used by the enemy AI's RTL.
Restore the header data bank after the callback returns.
Skip over the inline tail-jump helper to the post-AI checks.
Reload the current runtime slot for the callback.
Read the AI data bank from this slot.
Refresh the long pointer's bank byte before jumping.
Move that bank byte into the pushed word's high byte.
Push both bytes for the two bank-register pulls.
Discard the neighboring stored byte.
Select the enemy's AI data bank.
Tail-jump to AI; its RTL returns through the earlier JSL frame.
Recheck global frozen time after AI may have changed game state.
Include the debug enemy freeze flag in that post-AI check.
Frozen time skips frame-counter and instruction updates.
Advance this slot's frame counter on the eligible post-AI path.
Property bit $2000 enables processing the enemy's instruction list.
Leave the script untouched when that property bit is clear.
Mark instruction processing as stage 2 for this debug build path.
Advance scripts only after the selected AI has run.
Inspect paralysis again on all paths reaching the post-AI section.
This $0001 test is separate from the earlier pre-AI branch.
A flash timer of one triggers the paralysis death path.
If not, check the frozen timer for the same terminal value.
Skip that death path unless either timer equals one.
Clear the per-slot tile/spawn word used by this death path.
Invoke enemy death with A = 0 on the paralysis terminal-timer path.
An extended spritemap bypasses the ordinary visibility helper.
Use the radius-padded horizontal and fixed-margin vertical visibility tests.
A zero result allows drawing checks to continue.
Skip queue insertion for a failed ordinary visibility test.
Reload main properties after AI and possible death processing.
Bits $0100/$0200 block drawing-queue insertion.
Do not enqueue invisible or deletion-marked enemies.
Bit 0 of the drawing-disable flag also blocks queue insertion.
Queue this slot for later sprite drawing; do not emit OAM here.
Check the enemy's flash timer after the draw decision.
Global frozen time prevents this flash-timer tick.
Keep the flash timer unchanged on a frozen-time pass.
Tick the flash timer on the eligible path.
Test the updated timer against eight using the original branch condition.
Keep the hurt-AI bit while the timer takes this branch.
Clear only bit 1, the hurt-AI selector bit.
Preserve the remaining AI flags.
Advance the active-list cursor by the first byte of its word entry.
Complete the two-byte advance to the next active entry.
Process the next scheduled slot.
Service sprite objects on the common tail, including the early no-population exit.
Count executions of this routine, not hardware NMI events.
Use $FFFF for the four cleared solid-enemy collision slot indices.
Finish clearing the last directional collision index.
Clear the following four bookkeeping words.
Use the current runtime slot selected by EnemyIndex.
Read the per-enemy AI flags before ticking its script timer.
The frozen-AI bit blocks instruction processing independently of global time.
Return without decrementing the instruction timer when that bit is set.
Pre-decrement the word-sized instruction timer.
Only a zero result fetches script words; other results take the no-update path.
Read one byte early so the AI bank byte occupies the word's high byte.
Push that word to select the script's data bank.
Discard the byte preceding Enemy.bank.
Select the bank containing this enemy's instruction data.
Use Y as the current instruction-list cursor.
Fetch the next word from the instruction stream.
A clear sign bit identifies a duration/spritemap record.
A set sign bit supplies the command word; the caller supplied the bank byte.
Advance past the two-byte command word.
Push bank $A0 for the command's synthetic long return frame.
Push the loop return word minus one for the command's RTL.
Run the bank-local command through the shared long pointer.
Use the nonnegative word as the next instruction duration.
Read the spritemap word immediately following the duration.
Install that spritemap for the current enemy.
Advance from this duration/spritemap pair to its following record.
Each graphical record occupies four bytes.
Save the next instruction-list position.
Set the extra-property sign bit after accepting a graphical record.
Restore the entry data bank on the shared early/command exit.
RTS returns to the near caller of the interpreter.
Keep the current sprite when the pre-decremented timer was nonzero.
Clear the graphical-update marker on this no-update path.
Store the remaining extra properties unchanged.
Check the current runtime slot while preserving the caller's X.
Pad the left horizontal test by the enemy's X radius.
Compare the padded enemy position with the camera origin.
Reject this test when the subtraction result is negative.
Use the same $100-pixel viewport width as the normal activity scan.
Pad the right boundary by the enemy's X radius.
Reject the far horizontal test on a negative result.
Allow eight pixels above the camera's Y origin.
Reject the upper vertical test on a negative result.
Use camera Y plus $F8 as the lower vertical boundary.
Reject the lower vertical test on a negative result.
Return A = 0 and set Z when all four tests pass.
Return A = 1 and clear Z when a test fails.
Use the slot selected by EnemyIndex.
Read the enemy's drawing-layer index.
Convert the layer number to a word-table byte offset.
Keep that offset for updating the selected queue's size.
Read the base address of this layer's drawing queue.
Add its current byte size to find the insertion address.
Use Y as that queue insertion address.
Append the runtime slot offset rather than an enemy ID.
Write one word to the selected layer's queue.
Recover the layer's word-table offset.
Advance that queue's byte size by one of the entry's two bytes.
Finish advancing its size by two; drawing happens later.
Read the destination word at the command's parameter cursor.
Use that address as the interpreter's next Y cursor.
Resume the interpreter loop through its synthetic long return.
Read the command's loop-counter parameter word.
Store the loop counter, not the frame-duration timer.
Consume the first byte of the parameter word.
Consume its second byte before returning to command dispatch.
Continue interpreting commands in the same processing call.
Pre-decrement the enemy's separate loop-counter word.
For a nonzero result, reuse the goto command with the current parameter cursor.
A zero result skips the goto target's first byte.
Skip its second byte and continue with the following command.
Resume command interpretation in the same call.
Rewind Y to the sleep command's own word.
Prepare that command address for saving.
Leave the saved instruction cursor pointing at sleep.
Remove the interpreter loop's synthetic return word, retaining its bank byte.
Replace it with the interpreter's shared exit word minus one.
RTL exits this interpreter call instead of looping through another command.
Read the wait duration at the parameter cursor.
Set the frame-duration timer without replacing the spritemap.
Advance past the wait parameter's two bytes.
Save the cursor following this wait parameter.
Resume from that saved cursor on a future eligible timer expiry.
Remove the loop return word but keep its synthetic bank byte.
Substitute the interpreter's shared exit word minus one.
Terminate this interpreter call through that replacement return.
Read the current property flags before requesting deletion.
Set deletion bit $0200 without clearing the other flags.
Mark the slot for the activity scan to clear; do not clear its ID here.
Remove the command loop's synthetic return word.
Redirect the command's RTL to the interpreter's shared exit.
End script processing for this call; deletion is handled by the later scan.
